From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{2t}} & =\frac{1}{s-2},\,s>2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by applying the inverse Laplace transform to the above result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{2t}} & =\frac{1}{s-2} \\ {L}^{-1}{L{{e}^{2t}}} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-2}} \\ {e}^{2t} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-2}} \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-2}} & ={e}^{2t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the multiplicative property of the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4\cdot {L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-2}}=4\cdot {e}^{2t} \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{4}{s-2}}=4{e}^{2t}.\end{aligned}
$$
